unit_result_entry.title: Conditional metric and formally Hermitian representatives
unit_result_entry.why_material: Assuming the momentum operator is symmetric on the eventual domain, the source computes an adjoint relation with a nonnegative metric based on sin-squared of half the momentum, then discusses similarity transforms yielding a Hamiltonian with a quantum-anomaly momentum term or the Berry-Keating dilation Hamiltonian. It also records the decisive obstruction that the inverse metric is unbounded.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: This page is physically interleaved by two-column extraction. The construction depends on the unproved domain-level symmetry of momentum, and standard bounded-metric isospectral criteria do not directly apply because the inverse is unbounded; the authors instead claim a direct calculation.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: All metric, adjoint, rho, and transformed-Hamiltonian formulas should be checked against the retained PDF. Accepted content is restricted to the prose-supported conditional construction and its stated unbounded-inverse limitation.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Modified parity-time reflection gives a conditional spectral-reality route
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: After interchanging the usual roles assigned to coordinate and momentum, the source defines PT to fix x and reverse p, making iH invariant. It then uses the broken/unbroken PT eigenvalue alternatives to state that maximal breaking for iH would make the spectrum of H real, while distinguishing the behavior asserted for nontrivial and trivial zero states.

unit_result_entry.why_material: The discussion identifies the domain of H and establishment of self-adjointness as difficult open problems. The boundary-condition revisit further notes that finite-dimensional biorthogonality logic does not automatically pass to the infinite-dimensional setting: completeness of the proposed eigenstates is needed to identify the displayed operator as the Hermitian adjoint.

neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The source separates its formal Hamiltonian analysis from ordinary quantum mechanics because the states are not normalizable, then proposes a symmetric multiplicative cutoff, logarithmic state renormalization, and a limit.
